questions.q: Two vectors make a 60° angle. Vector 1 has length 2 and vector 2 has length 3. What are the dot product and the cosine similarity?
questions.explain: Dot $= 2 \cdot 3 \cdot \cos 60° = 3$; cosine similarity divides by both lengths: $3 / (2 \cdot 3) = 0.5$.

questions.q: You double the length of Vector 2 without changing the angle. What happens?
options: The cosine similarity doubles; the dot product stays the same
The dot product doubles; the cosine similarity stays the same
Both the dot product and the cosine similarity double
questions.explain: Cosine similarity ignores length — it only depends on the angle. The plain dot product grows with the lengths.

questions.q: What is the cosine similarity of two vectors pointing in exactly opposite directions (180°)?
questions.explain: $\cos 180° = -1$: total disagreement. 0 is for perpendicular vectors, 1 for the same direction.

questions.q: Why do the length sliders on this page start at 0.5 instead of 0?
options: Lengths below 0.5 make the cosine larger than 1
Cosine similarity is undefined for the zero vector (division by zero)
questions.explain: The formula divides by $\|\mathbf{v}_1\|\,\|\mathbf{v}_2\|$; a zero-length vector would make that 0.
